claim: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a rare genetic disease caused by mutations of the X-linked gene methyl-CpG-binding protein2 (MECP2) in more than 95% of patients.
source: Rett syndrome (RTT), is a rare genetic disease caused by mutations of the X-linked gene methyl-CpG-binding protein2 (MECP2), in more than 95% of patients (Amir et al., 1999; Chahrour and Zoghbi, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Amir et al., 1999 and Chahrour and Zoghbi, 2007.

claim: RTT affected subjects, almost exclusively females, show progressive loss of acquired motor and cognitive skills.
source: Affected subjects, almost exclusively females, show progressive loss of acquired motor and cognitive skills and develop additional symptoms including stereotypic hand movements, drug-resistant seizures, breathing and autonomic dysfunctions (Chahrour and Zoghbi, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chahrour and Zoghbi, 2007.

claim: RTT affected subjects develop stereotypic hand movements, drug-resistant seizures, breathing and autonomic dysfunctions.
source: Affected subjects, almost exclusively females, show progressive loss of acquired motor and cognitive skills and develop additional symptoms including stereotypic hand movements, drug-resistant seizures, breathing and autonomic dysfunctions (Chahrour and Zoghbi, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chahrour and Zoghbi, 2007.

claim: Increased cholesterol plasma levels have been found in RTT individuals carrying MECP2 mutations.
source: Increased cholesterol plasma levels and changes in the activity/expression of genes and proteins involved in the cellular uptake, synthesis and feedback regulation of circulating cholesterol have recently been found in RTT individuals carrying MECP2 mutations (Grillo et al., 2013; Justice et al., 2013; Segatto et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Grillo et al., 2013; Justice et al., 2013; Segatto et al., 2014.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Grillo et al., 2013; Justice et al., 2013; Segatto et al., 2014.

claim: Only one-third of RTT patients show elevated levels of plasma cholesterol.

claim: Cholesterol homeostasis is important for central nervous system function.
source: Cholesterol homeostasis is important for central nervous system function and defects in cholesterol synthesis may cause neurologic symptoms (Waterham, 2006).

claim: Defects in cholesterol synthesis may cause neurologic symptoms.

claim: Inactivation of Sqle improved motor deficit and enhanced survival in Mecp2-null mice.
source: The relationship between RTT and cholesterol is supported by recent findings showing that inactivation of Sqle, encoding squalene epoxidase, a key enzyme in the synthesis of cholesterol (Pfrieger and Ungerer, 2011), and pharmacological treatment with the cholesterol lowering drugs statins improved motor deficit and enhanced survival in Mecp2-null mice (Buchovecky et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Buchovecky et al., 2013.

claim: Pharmacological treatment with statins improved motor deficit and enhanced survival in Mecp2-null mice.
